messages.subject: SPDE parameters
parts:
Hi all,

I developed Model 1 with constant spatial field: f(s, model=spde) 
and Model 2 with spatial field changed over year: f(s, model=spde, replicate=s.repl).

And got marginal posterior distributions for parameters in the spatial field (please see attachment). 
Plot (a-d) are marginal posterior distributions for parameters from Model 1;
plot (e-h) are marginal posterior distributions for parameters from Model 2.

Obviously, they are different. But how can I interpret these differences on each parameter from the two models?

Thanks,
Ruby

messages.author: 17f8070912132195
messages.subject: Re: SPDE parameters
parts:
For better visualization, I plot marginal posterior distribution for the same parameter from two models in one plot. Full line for M2,  dash line for M3. 

The major questions include:
1. why the posterior mean of the variance from M3 is larger than that from M2?
My answer: when separating the data to different years, each year has limited observations, which could increase the spatial variance.
Is it correct?
2. why the posterior mean of the range(rho) from M3 is larger than that from M2?
Totally no idea.

Thanks in advance!

On 10 Aug 2017, at 06:03, Rujia Bi <crysta...@gmail.com> wrote:

Intercept, some fixed effects, random year effect (RW2)

The parameters often need to be considered together; e.g., the spde variance parameter and the observation variance need to be considered, as they necessarily interact differently in different models.

The number of observations doesn't impact the field variance as such. The number of observations would rather have an effect on the uncertainties.
But on possible interpretation is that the the non-replicated model you are essentially modeling the temporally averaged version of the fields in the replication model, which should be expected to have a smaller variance. But this then interacts with the observation variance, as well as the correlation range parameter, so it's not trivial to interpret.

Finn
